page: Amazon Web Services r7iz.2xlarge is a memory-optimized server powered by an Intel Xeon 6455B processor with an x86_64 architecture. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. The processor runs at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz and includes 60 MB of L3 cache. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. It utilizes the AWS Nitro hypervisor. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance, and the baseline network bandwidth is 3 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates top-tier single-core performance, scoring 2226.0 in Geekbench single-core tests and 2903.0 in Geekbench text processing, both placing in the top 10% tier. Single-threaded gzip compression at 34.55 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 14.85 GB/sec fall into the top 25% tier. Multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics generally align with average mid-tier performance, including a multi-core Geekbench score of 8490.0 and uncached large-block memory read speeds of 70.75 GB/sec. Redis SET operations reach 10.89 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput is recorded at 16.19 GB/sec.

The qualitative cost efficiency of the r7iz.2xlarge is defined by its high-speed DDR5 memory and high-frequency CPU cores, which offer strong single-threaded execution without requiring a massive vCPU footprint. However, tradeoffs include the complete absence of local NVMe storage and a modest baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps. This server is optimized for workloads requiring high memory capacity per core and fast single-core execution, such as database operations, memory-intensive applications, software compilation, and lightweight text or language model processing.
